message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing or not in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. So, my mom and dad are both away for a while. My mom is in another state for a class thing, and my dad is on a business trip. That leaves me, my sister, and my brother at home. My sister is 18, I'm 17, and my brother is 12. My parents decided to leave my sister "in charge" while they're gone. I guess that means she's supposed to take care of us and make sure everything runs smoothly. But here's the thing: my sister has a tendency to let the power go to her head. She can usually make my little brother obey her, but when it comes to me, she has a tougher time. I mean, I respect her, but I'm not exactly going to let her boss me around just because she's older. So, on Sunday, I had plans to go out with my girlfriend for dinner. I was really looking forward to it. But my sister stopped me and told me I couldn't leave. When I asked why, she just said, "Because I said so." At first, I thought she was joking, so I laughed it off. But she wasn't laughing; she was serious. I told her that she can boss my little brother around, but she can't boss me. I went out with my girlfriend anyway. When I came home, my little brother had apparently heard the commotion and called my mom, telling her that we were "fighting." My mom called me and said that I'm grounded and have to do what my sister says because she's "in charge." I tried to protest, but she wasn't having it. She grounded me for disobeying my sister, who is acting like a pseudo-parent while they're away. I just dropped it because it's not worth arguing with my mom. But now I'm wondering, did I do the right thing? Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Ass) for leaving to see my girlfriend when my sister told me not to? First, I need to consider the dynamics of the situation. My sister is 18, and I'm 17. She's technically older, but we're both still teenagers. My parents left her in charge, which gives her some authority, but how much authority should she really have? Is it fair for her to dictate where I can and can't go? On one hand, my sister is supposed to be in charge, so maybe I should have respected her decision. But on the other hand, she's not a parent, and her authority is limited. Plus, she's only a year older than me, so the age difference isn't that big. I feel like I should have some say in my own plans, especially if they don't pose any real risk. Another thing to consider is how my sister handles authority. She can make my little brother obey her, but with me, it's different. Maybe she's trying to assert her authority too much, and that's why she's being so strict. But does that give her the right to control my actions? Also, my little brother told my mom about the "fight," which led to me being grounded. I forgave him because he's just a kid, but it's still frustrating that my mom took his word without hearing my side of the story. So, is it AITA for me to have gone out with my girlfriend despite my sister's objections? I think it depends on a few factors. First, did I understand the rules before I decided to go out? If my sister had clearly established that I couldn't leave the house, then maybe I should have respected that. But if it was just a casual request, then maybe I wasn't obligated to follow it. Second, was my sister's reasoning valid? She just said, "Because I said so," which doesn't really hold much weight. If she had given a legitimate reason, like there was something important I needed to do at home, then I might have reconsidered. But without a real explanation, it's hard to take her seriously. Third, what were the consequences of my actions? I got grounded, which is a punishment, but I also had to listen to my sister, who I don't think is equipped to handle that kind of responsibility. It seems like my mom is putting too much pressure on my sister by making her "in charge." In the end, I think I did what I thought was right for me. I wanted to go out with my girlfriend, and I didn't see a good reason to cancel those plans. However, I also understand that my sister was trying to fulfill the role my parents gave her, even if she wasn't entirely suited for it. Maybe in the future, I can communicate better with her and set some boundaries so that both of us feel respected. Overall, I don't think I'm entirely in the wrong, but I could have handled the situation differently to avoid conflict and better respect the authority my parents have given my sister.
